messages:
maria: Heads up — found an onboarding leak in the Go generator sampleapp. When auth refresh happens mid-stream the iterator goroutine doesn't exit. Repro: run `./examples/generator --stream --refresh-every=5s` then rotate token.

sam: can you paste a tiny repro or the stack? short ones help.

maria: paste logs:
```
INFO: handshake ok
WARN: auth refresh triggered
INFO: client sent cancel
INFO: generator returned err: auth: token expired
<--- but the process keeps running, goroutine count doesn't drop --->
goroutine 42 [chan receive]:
  internal/gen/stream.recvLoop(...)
```

kevin: this sounds like the classic auth-refresh -> handshake retry path where the recv loop is waiting on an internal channel that never closes. we don't propagate ctx cancellation into `Next()` today.

olga: file reference? where in sampleapp is that?

maria: examples/generator/stream.go around the iterator wrapper. snippet: 
```go
for {
  tok, err := gen.Next()
  if err != nil { break }
  process(tok)
}
```
Next() is blocking; Close() exists but caller needs to call it explicitly. if auth refresh happens inside SDK, Close() isn't invoked by the SDK on handshake failure.

sam: so ergonomics problem: Next() has no ctx. parity issue with other SDKs that accept context on pull APIs. also makes onboarding sampleapp brittle.

kevin: two main options: (1) add `Next(ctx)` or `NextWith(ctx)`, (2) add an `Interrupt()`/`Abort()` helper that closes the channels from outside. both are breaking-ish for clients.

maria: my vote: add `Next(ctx)` and keep old `Next()` as convenience; document cancellation semantics. New method unblocks on ctx.Done() and returns ctx.Err().

dev-bot: draft design doc pinned: https://redwood.ai/design/gen-ctx-ergonomics (WIP). Please add reproduction steps. :memo:

olga: another dimension — auth middleware retries are silent in sampleapp which makes it hard to spot mid-stream 401->refresh->handshake. add a debug flag or an event log entry for auth flow.

sam: workaround for now: spawn `Next()` in a goroutine and select on ctx.Done() to call `gen.Close()` from the parent. ugly but effective. e.g.
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
ch := make(chan error, 1)
go func() { _, err := gen.Next(); ch <- err }()
select { case <-ctx.Done(): gen.Close(); case <-ch: }
```

kevin: thanks. i'll sketch a tiny RFC and prototype PR with `Next(ctx)` and sampleapp changes (debug auth + docs). @maria @olga wanna coauthor?

maria: yep, i'll add the repro and trace logs to the PR.

olga: i'll update sampleapp to enable verbose auth logging behind `--auth-debug`. won't change default behavior.

sam: ack. once PR is up we should run quick perf microbench to ensure `Next(ctx)` doesn't add allocation/regress for the no-ctx case.

maria: noted. thanks all. i'll open the issue with a minimal repro and link the logs. :+1:
